knowledge_ref: # Which technique cell each GO detector's knowledge-ref belongs to. YARA rules carry their own
# `shellsight_cells` meta; Go detectors cannot, so the mapping lives here.
# DIRECTION MATTERS. The cells were derived from retrieved prior art in taxonomy.yaml FIRST, and
# these detectors were mapped onto them afterwards. Deriving the cells from the detectors would make
# coverage a tautology -- every technique we detect would appear covered.
# Each row was assigned by reading what the rule DOES in internal/phptaint/taint.go, not by reading
# its name. `sink-on-request` is the clearest reason why: the name suggests one cell and the code
# covers five, because eval, include/require and `new ReflectionFunction(...)->invoke()` are all
# language constructs it handles in separate branches under one ref.
# perlpytaint speaks for THREE languages from one row -- detectors.GO_PACKAGE_LANGUAGES maps
# the package to perl, python and cgi -- so this row carries every language's cells together
# and V2 checks each kit against the prefix that belongs to it. Perl's four were assigned by
# reading perlSinks in taint.go, not the ref's name: the pass implements system, exec,
# backtick, qx, piped-open and string-eval, and has NO two-arg-open sink, so
# perl/dispatch/two-arg-open-injection is deliberately absent and is a measured gap.
perlpytaint:sink-on-request
# asptaint speaks for TWO languages -- `cmd/diskprobe` gates the pass on `ctxASP || ctxASPX` -- so,
# like perlpytaint above, one row carries both kits' cells and V2 checks each against its own prefix.
# Assigned by reading `internal/asptaint/taint.go`, not the ref's name. The four `asp/channel/*`
# cells are the named alternatives of `sourceExpr`; `executeglobal` and `scriptcontrol` are separate
# sink entries; `eval-request` is the `direct` branch and `eval-request-indirect` is the propagation
# the pass was built for. `session-staged` is covered through `elemAssignRe`, which taints the
# container NAME on `Session("x") = Request("y")`.
# THREE THINGS ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT, because the code does not do them and a cell that reads as
# covered while its construct is unimplemented is the most expensive error in this table:
#   - `aspx/channel/request-body`: `BinaryRead`/`TotalBytes` are sources but `InputStream` -- the
#     .NET-idiomatic spelling, and 47/475 of the aspx candidate pool -- is not. 2 of 3 markers is
#     not coverage.
#   - every `aspx/surface/*` cell: the pass PARSES the WebHandler surface, it does not assert it.
#   - `aspx/family/china-chopper`: findings carry `Family: "GenericWebshell"`; the pass attributes
#     nothing. Four of the closed gap items are China Chopper, and it still is not this pass's claim.
asptaint:sink-on-request
phptaint:sink-on-request
phptaint:com-exec-on-request
phptaint:callback-on-request
phptaint:request-tainted-callback
phptaint:unbound-callback-dispatch
phptaint:dynamic-dispatch-on-request
phptaint:direct-invoke-built-callable
phptaint:forwarder-obfuscated-callee
phptaint:decode-loop-dispatch
phptaint:nibble-assembler-loop
phptaint:arbitrary-file-write
phptaint:file-drop-on-request
